chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ali al-Taflisi narrated to me from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Hamadani from Muhammad b. Ali al-Hadi from Ali b. Musa al-Rida from Imam Musa b. Jafar from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from al-Baqir Muhammad b. Ali from the Master of Worshipers Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of the Youth of Paradise al-Husayn from the Master of Deputies Ali (peace be upon him) from the Master of Prophets Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family). He said:

Do not look to the plenitude of their prayers, their fasting, their pilgrimages, their good works, and their recitation at night. Look to the honesty of their words and the fulfillment of their trusts.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about judging people by their prayers versus their honesty?
ai.summary: Through a golden chain (silsilat al-dhahab) passing through all twelve Imams, the Prophet Muhammad (S) teaches that outward religious acts -- abundant prayers, fasting, pilgrimage, charity, and nighttime devotion -- should not be the measure of a person's worth. Instead, the true criteria are honesty of speech and trustworthiness in fulfilling obligations.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. `Ali al-Taflisi narrated to me from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Hamadani from Muhammad b. `Ali al-Hadi from `Ali b. Musa al-Rida from Imam Musa b. Ja`far from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from al-Baqir Muhammad b. `Ali from the Master of Worshipers `Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of the Youth of Paradise al-Husayn from the Master of Deputies `Ali (as) from the Masters of Prophets Muhammad (s). He said:

Do not look to the plenitude of their prayers, their fasting, their pilgrimages, their good works, and their recitation at night. Look to the honesty of their words and the fulfillment of their trusts.
